explanation: The fellowship honors exceptional artists, and Burns received it "because of his lifetime contributions to the arts," so he was selected for it: "chosen." "Ineligible" contradicts the fact that he received the award, and nothing in the text suggests he was confused or reluctant.

Alexander "was very busy," took a desk in an office, and avoided social clubs, so being at work "almost constantly" means working nearly all the time without a break: "nonstop." "Quickly" is about speed, not how much of the time he worked, and "cautiously" and "enough" don't fit the picture of a man buried in work.

explanation: "Whereas" sets up a contrast with "intensified": people are decisive when information flow is intensified but slow when it is the opposite, "reduced." "Evaluated," "determined," and "acquired" are not opposites of intensified, so they don't complete the contrast.

The next sentence says the Mexica could "precisely identify" the dates of solstices, so they tracked time with great precision, or "exactitude." "Resilience" means toughness and "precariousness" means instability; neither matches the emphasis on precision.

Before the underlined sentence, the text sets up the question and describes the experiment with 3D glasses. The underlined sentence then reports what the cuttlefish did and what that suggests, which is the study's result. It doesn't propose future research (B), and the reason cuttlefish were thought to lack 3D vision is never explained (D).

fix.passage: Horses and toads can see in three dimensions (3D), which helps them perceive distance and depth. Octopuses and squid are thought to lack 3D vision. Many researchers once thought the same about cuttlefish, but Trevor Wardill and his team wanted to test whether this assumption was true. The team studied how cuttlefish wearing 3D glasses reacted to 3D images of shrimp (a favorite prey) projected on a tank wall. <u>Cuttlefish changed their striking position to match the 3D images, suggesting that their vision is more like that of horses and toads than that of octopuses or squid.</u>

explanation: Population density and physical fitness are what "some studies emphasize," but the text then says walking decisions involve "multiple conditions and needs," so these factors are only a few among many. The text never says people rarely consider them (B) or that they have been overemphasized (C), and it doesn't limit them to Boston (D).

fix.passage: Boston has high pedestrian traffic, but simply replicating a feature of Boston associated with walkability—e.g., its high number of intersections—may be insufficient to induce increased walking in other cities. As urbanist Mariela Alfonzo argues, our understanding of individuals’ decision-making about whether to walk is insufficiently robust: some studies emphasize the role of population density, others the role of individual physical fitness, and so on, but walking decisions are made in complex contexts in which multiple conditions and needs inform individuals’ choices.

choices.C: They identify factors that Alfonzo argues have been overemphasized in studies of decision-making about walking but that the text asserts are relevant to most people’s walking decisions.

There is no Frigate like a Book

The verb's subject is "a writing technique," which is singular, and the sentence describes what the technique generally does, so the singular present-tense "creates" is needed. "Create," "are creating," and "have created" are all plural forms.
After "more likely," English uses an infinitive: "more likely to eat." The other forms ("ate," "still be eating," "eaten") can't follow "likely" directly and leave the sentence ungrammatical.

The text describes a general, ongoing situation in the present tense ("have a clear difference," "require"), so the present-tense "struggle" keeps the tenses consistent. The past forms "struggled," "were struggling," and "had struggled" would wrongly place a timeless fact in the past.

"Painter" is a title-like description directly before the name, so no commas separate "painter" from "Gani Odutokun" (the name is essential here), and no punctuation should come between the subject and its verb "was." A and D add unnecessary commas, and B puts a period in the middle of the sentence.

"She was not alone in her efforts, however" is a complete sentence, and "Fernando Orejuela ... contributed to the project" is another, so a semicolon is needed after "however" to join them. "However" belongs with the first clause, since it contrasts with the previous sentence. B and D create run-ons, and C puts "however" in the wrong clause.

The two clauses present contrasting findings side by side: negative adjectives change fastest, while negative nouns change slowest. "Meanwhile" introduces a contrasting fact considered at the same time. "Similarly" would wrongly suggest the same pattern, "hence" implies cause and effect, and "subsequently" implies a time sequence.

explanation: The text lists traits both groups have (spines, pointed snouts, small size) and says they developed them independently, so hedgehog tenrecs share "similarities with" true hedgehogs. Bird-Walton's place in memory is compared with that of a famous "first," whose deed will "always be remembered." The contrast implies Bird-Walton's place is less secure, or "uncertain." "Enduring" and "conspicuous" say the opposite, and "deserving" doesn't fit the comparison about how well someone is remembered.

Robots are made humanlike so people find them easier to interact with, and "to that end" features like walking on two legs strengthen people's comfort; "buttress" means to support or reinforce. "Mitigate" (lessen) is the main trap because it means the opposite, and "constrict" and "repudiate" would also weaken comfort.

The sentence contrasts what scholarship has undermined with what is "indisputable": Ibn Rushd's works were mostly available far from the center of Islamic thought, which might suggest other philosophers ignored them. So the undermined claim is that his works were unimportant to his peers, "inconsequential to" them. "Imitated by" would mean influence, which wouldn't create the needed contrast, and "controversial among" and "antagonistic toward" have no support in the text.

The text first defines community science, then lists its benefits (public awareness, learning for youth, more data), and finally mentions the butterfly study that used it. That is exactly B. The text doesn't give the study's results (A), suggest future projects (C), or discuss public opinion (D).

Text 1 says Wahbi's team did not use barriers, the "crucial step" for excluding other pathways, so their study didn't isolate the CMN. Text 2 argues that even Xiao's barriers can't rule out other pathways, so a study without barriers certainly couldn't. Both authors would answer B with "no." They would disagree about A, since Text 1 thinks Xiao's barriers worked and Text 2 does not.

fix.passage:
Text 1
In separate studies, Yanbo Xiao and colleagues and Sana Wahbi and colleagues examined whether plants transfer nutrients to one another using a common mycorrhizal network (CMN)—a lattice of fungal strands in the soil. Xiao and colleagues excluded all pathways other than the CMN by using barriers to keep the plants’ root systems separate while allowing mycorrhizal strands through—a crucial step Wahbi and colleagues’ study did not take.

Text 2
Xiao and colleagues took the necessary precaution of separating the plants’ root systems (thereby excluding root-to-root transmission). However, any barrier used must allow the threadlike hyphae of a CMN to pass through, and this permeability would also allow liquids through. Thus, the researchers’ experimental design cannot ensure that any nutrient transfer observed can be attributed to a CMN and not to some other pathway.

choices.A: Are the barriers used in Xiao and colleagues’ study sufficient to ensure that nutrient transfer could only occur via a CMN?
choices.B: Did Wahbi and colleagues’ study effectively exclude any nutrient pathway other than a CMN?

explanation: The text names one limit: Places API data mostly include customer-facing places. fix.passage: Researchers Cesar A. Hidalgo, Elisa Castaner, and Andres Sevtsuk created a computer model to predict the mix of businesses and places of interest found in a given neighborhood. The team used data from the Google Places API service to help identify movie theaters, gyms, and other businesses and map their locations. This approach has some limits—data from Places API tend to be restricted to places that are customer facing—but the data set nonetheless provides an extremely reliable source to study colocation patterns of neighborhood amenities.

"Accordingly" signals this consequence. "However" signals a contrast, and "moreover" and "similarly" just add a point rather than draw a conclusion.
